groups.heading: config: hosts was REJECTED, now ACCEPTED

answers.why: Probed: the oracle (zod 3) rejects hosts=["2459::52d2%lo0"] while the merged build accepts it, so inputs flip reject->accept (looser). The cause is visible in a second probe: zod 3's z.string().ip() accepted a %zone suffix ONLY on fe80: link-local addresses (oracle accepts fe80::1%eth0 but rejects 2459::52d2%lo0 and 2001:db8::ff00:42:8329%wlan0), because its ipv6 regex had a single fe80 branch. src/schemas.ts replaces that with a generic refine that splits on '%' and validates the left half with z.ipv6(), i.e. it accepts a zone index on ANY IPv6 address. review/corpus-diffs.md section [4] signs off the OPPOSITE direction (fe80::1%eth0 was accepted by zod 3 and rejected by zod 4, hence KEEP OLD) and explicitly asserts the union 'reproduces exactly the set zod 3 matched ... nothing *new* is let in' - the probe shows that assertion is false, so this widening (508 of 1795 diffs) was never reviewed. No stored-value diffs here: every example is a verdict flip. Judgement: real_clients=yes - the same client-side formatting that produced the real fe80::1%eth0 caller in the corpus emits '<addr>%<ifname>' for whatever address an interface has, and hosts is operator-supplied config; so plausible input now slips past the check zod 4 itself would apply. Judgement: a human must either narrow the zone branch to fe80::/10 (restoring zod 3 exactly, as the doc claims) or accept the widening deliberately.

claims.claim: The merged build accepts a config host with an IPv6 zone index that zod 3 rejected (2459::52d2%lo0).
zod 3 accepted a %zone suffix only on fe80: link-local addresses, so the merged refine accepts strictly more than zod 3 (the doc's 'nothing new is let in' is wrong).
claims.expect: G508b zod3 fe80=true zod3 lo0=false zod3 global=false

groups.heading: config: timeoutMs was ACCEPTED, now REJECTED

answers.why: Probed: oracle accepts timeoutMs=Infinity and stores it (a.value.timeoutMs===Infinity), the merged build rejects with 'timeoutMs: Invalid input: expected number, received Infinity' - zod 4's z.number() requires a finite number, zod 3 only excluded NaN. So a verdict flip accept->reject (stricter); no input is accepted by both with a different stored value. review/corpus-diffs.md covers ip, name, age and a list of silent API moves; it never mentions non-finite numbers or timeoutMs, so this is not signed off (read_file evidence, not a probe). Judgement: real_clients=no - JSON cannot carry Infinity (JSON.stringify({timeoutMs:Infinity}) emits null, probed), and src/schemas.ts documents Config as 'usually read from environment variables (so: strings)', so a well-behaved client cannot produce this value; the fuzzer injects it directly. Judgement: the tightening also closes a latent bug, since zod 3 would happily store an infinite timeout, so I see no action beyond noting it - but note the flip is real, not a message-only difference.

claims.claim: zod 3 accepts and stores timeoutMs=Infinity; the merged build rejects it.
The rejection is zod 4's finiteness check on z.number(), and Infinity is not representable in JSON, so a JSON client cannot send it.

groups.heading: signup: ip was REJECTED, now ACCEPTED

answers.why: Same root cause as the hosts group, on the signup.ip field. Probed: oracle rejects ip="3d62::9037%1", merged build accepts it; oracle also rejects ip="::%1" (a zone on the unspecified address) while the merged build accepts that too; both versions accept fe80::1%eth0. So the merged zonedIpv6 refine is wider than zod 3's .ip(), which only matched %zone on fe80: addresses. review/corpus-diffs.md [4] signed off restoring the fe80 case (accepted->rejected) and claims the union lets in nothing new; the probe contradicts that, so these 357 reject->accept flips are an unreviewed widening. No stored-value diffs in this group (verdict flips only). Judgement: real_clients=yes for the plausible part - a client that renders scope ids will post '<addr>%<iface>' for non-link-local addresses as well, and those are now stored as valid ip values that zod 4's own z.ipv6() rejects; '::%1' in the same group is clearly junk and shows the refine is wider than the doc intends. Judgement: a human should decide between an fe80-only zone branch (faithful KEEP OLD) and accepting any zoned address on purpose.

claims.claim: The merged build accepts signup ip=3d62::9037%1, which zod 3 rejects.
The widening is not limited to meaningful link-local input: '::%1' is newly accepted, while the signed-off fe80::1%eth0 case is accepted by both versions.
claims.expect: G357b empty_addr oracle=false main=true | fe80 oracle=true main=true

groups.heading: signup: age was ACCEPTED, now REJECTED

answers.why: Probed: oracle accepts age=1e+21 and age=9007199254740994, the merged build rejects both with 'age: Too big: expected int to be <=9007199254740991' - zod 3's .int() was Number.isInteger (true for any integral float), zod 4's .int() means safe integer and bounds the value by +/-MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Every example in the group (1e21, 9007199254740994, 1e30, 1152921504606847000, 1.79e308, 1.7976931348623145e+308) is above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so the group is exactly one change. review/corpus-diffs.md section [2] 'age - was ACCEPTED, now REJECTED' describes this same change (same mechanism, same message, examples 1e+21 and 9007199254740992) and records 'Recommendation: ACCEPT NEW - left as zod 4 behaves; no code change' - so a human signed off this exact behaviour (read_file evidence). Judgement: real_clients=no - none of these values is an age, above 2^53 the float grid is coarser than 1 so the stored number would already be lossy; the doc's suggested follow-up (a real .max(130)) stays a separate product change and is not a blocker for shipping.

claims.claim: age=1e+21 is accepted by zod 3 and rejected by the merged build with the safe-integer upper bound message.
claims.expect: G324 oracle=true main=false problem=age: Too big: expected int to be <=9007199254740991

claims.claim: The other examples are the same change: every rejected value exceeds Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.

groups.heading: signup: rejected by both, but different fields reported

answers.why: Probed: for a signup that is invalid in several places at once (bad email + zoned ip + oversized age) both versions reject - oracle reports fields email,ip and the merged build reports age,email. So no input changes verdict here and nothing is stored, only the set of reported field names moves. Every example in the group is the shadow of two other groups: 'ip' disappears from the list because zoned IPv6 is now accepted (the signup ip group) and 'age' appears because unsafe integers are now rejected (the age group). Judgement: already_signed_off=false in the strict sense - corpus-diffs.md discusses the ip and age changes themselves and notes that error *wording* is not compared, but it never addresses field-set shifts on already-rejected requests. Judgement: nothing to act on in this group by itself: the caller still gets a rejection either way, so the only decisions are the ones in the ip and age groups; the one caveat is that a client reading the first failing field would see a different field name. Judgement: real_clients=unknown - a real client can certainly send one invalid field, but these multi-field-invalid blobs look like generator artefacts rather than production traffic.

claims.claim: A multi-field-invalid signup is rejected by both versions but with different reported fields (oracle email,ip vs merged age,email).
Both versions reject the input, so there is no verdict change and no parsed value to compare.

groups.heading: config: rejected by both, but different fields reported

answers.why: Probed: a config with hosts=["2459::52d2%lo0","nope"] and timeoutMs=Infinity is rejected by both versions - oracle reports hosts.0,hosts.1 and the merged build reports hosts.1,timeoutMs. No verdict flip, nothing stored. Exactly like the signup field-set group, this is the shadow of two other groups: a hosts.N entry drops off because zoned IPv6 is now accepted (the hosts group) and timeoutMs appears because Infinity is now rejected (the timeoutMs group). Judgement: already_signed_off=false - corpus-diffs.md does not discuss field-set differences on configs that fail either way (and never mentions timeoutMs at all). Judgement: no separate action: the config is refused by both versions, so the decisions live in the hosts and timeoutMs groups; real_clients=unknown because some examples are driven only by host strings (plausible) while others require Infinity, which a JSON/env client cannot produce.

claims.claim: A config invalid in several places is rejected by both versions with different reported fields (oracle hosts.0,hosts.1 vs merged hosts.1,timeoutMs).
Both versions reject it, so the difference is only in which fields are named.

groups.heading: signup: website accepted, but the PARSED VALUE changed

answers.why: Probed: website=" https://example.com" is accepted by both versions, but zod 3 stores the string verbatim (length 20) and the merged build stores "https://example.com" (length 19); same for a trailing newline (length 20 -> 19, exact value "https://example.com"). So no verdict changes, but the persisted value differs - zod 4's z.url() runs the input through URL parsing, which strips leading/trailing whitespace and control characters. It is a trim, not full href normalisation: the merged build stores "https://example.com" without adding a trailing slash. review/corpus-diffs.md lists z.string().url() -> z.url() under 'Silent API moves (no corpus difference) ... pure API rename with no behavioural change', so this value rewrite was never signed off; the 400-request corpus simply happened to contain no whitespace-padded URL (read_file evidence). Judgement: real_clients=yes - copy-paste into a web form routinely adds a leading space or a trailing newline, so real signups will now be stored under a different website string than before, which matters for exact-match lookups, dedup and uniqueness keys, and for any row written before the upgrade. Judgement: trimming is probably the better behaviour, but it is a silent change of stored data that a human should confirm (and decide whether to normalise historic rows) rather than inherit from a dependency bump.

claims.claim: A leading-space URL is accepted by both versions but stored trimmed by the merged build (20 chars -> 19).
Same for a trailing newline; the merged build stores the bare origin with no trailing slash, i.e. the change is a whitespace trim.
